messages.subject: fitqtl: percent variance calculation?
parts:
Hello,

I couldn't find this on the discussion group and thought it was worth asking about.  I used data and a linkage map from a set of recombinant inbred lines (using convert2riself) and have performed a multiple qtl analysis (using the results of a scanone to seed a search of model space using stepwiseqtl, with penalties calculated based on 1000 permutations and additive only set to true). I then passed the result of stepwiseqtl to the fitqtl function to generate a drop one table.  When I try to calculate the percent variance explained (PVE) by each QTL in the drop one table by hand using the equation given in the description of the fitqtl function 1-10^(-2/n)LOD and the LOD score from the drop one table, I get very different percent variances than those in the drop one table. When I calculate percent variances by hand, the total adds up to >100%. I must be doing something wrong here or perhaps misunderstanding something. The two sets of percent variance explained have a correlation coefficient of >0.99 so I believe they are both getting at the same (relative) answer, however this is somewhat unsatisfying. Is fitqtl re-scaling PVE somehow? Can you please help me either trust the results of the fitqtl output or explain how percent variance could sum to >100% (and why I should trust those rather than the fitqtl output)?

For reference, all QTL are >100cM apart and so I do not think they are linked; a subsequent scantwo analysis for epsistasis did not identify any significant QTL-QTL interactions.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] fitqtl: percent variance calculation?
parts:
Looking at the code for fitqtl(), it seems that the equation being used is more complicated:

result[i,4] <- result.full[1,5] - 100*(1 - 10^(-2*z$lod/n.ind))

see https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/fitqtl.R#L852

that is, for the first QTL, 1.886% is derived as 85.64464 - 100*(1 - 10^(-2*(72.0753 - 4.582)/171))

where 85.64464 and 72.0753 are taken from the full model result.

The PVEs can sum to > 100% when the genotypes at the individual QTL are not exactly uncorrelated in the observed data.

karl
